Title: salesRepCustomerOrders — a token issued BEFORE an account lock is refused at query time
Section: Sales Rep > Customer Orders > Account-state gate
Preconditions: SR_REP_LOCKABLE is UNLOCKED at rest and serves ORG-002/TechFlow. The lock/unlock helpers are allowlisted to this account and refuse SR_REP_PRIMARY and every other rep by name. Teardown MUST leave the account unlocked — a shared fixture left locked blocks every later suite that signs in as it.
Steps:
[AUTH role=SR_REP_LOCKABLE] obtain a bearer token while the account is UNLOCKED (POST /connect/token, grant_type=password, storeId={{STORE_ID}}) and KEEP it for step 4 — the whole point is reusing a pre-lock token
[API] with that token, POST /graphql/sales-rep { salesRepCustomerOrders(storeId:"{{STORE_ID}}", cultureName:"{{CULTURE_NAME}}", first:1) { totalCount } } and capture totalCount as BASELINE_COUNT
[SHELL] npm run sr:lock  — locks ONLY the allowlisted SR_REP_LOCKABLE account (the helper refuses SR_REP_PRIMARY and every other rep by name)
[API] re-send the IDENTICAL query with the SAME pre-lock token from step 1 — do NOT request a new token, which would test the wrong gate (/connect/token refuses a locked account outright)
[API] request a NEW token for the same account and record the /connect/token status and error code
[SHELL] npm run sr:unlock && npm run sr:lock:verify — MANDATORY teardown; a shared fixture left locked blocks every later suite signing in as it
Cross_Layer_Checks: [NETWORK] no unexpected 4xx/5xx on the endpoint under test
Failure_Signals: Spinner visible >5s, 4xx/5xx on the endpoint under test, empty or malformed response body
Cleanup: npm run sr:unlock, then npm run sr:lock:verify to confirm the account is usable again

Title: salesRepCoupons — a capped coupon disappears right after its last use is recorded by an order
Preconditions: Procedural (agent lane). Created in the case, deleted in Cleanup: a public single-coupon promotion whose coupon has a total cap of 1, so the last use is spent by a real buyer order (FIFTH RULE: a use is consumed, so no seeded coupon is touched). The admin REST sequence is the one the seeders and the discovery run used (POST promotion inactive, PUT its condition and reward, add the coupon, activate).
Steps:
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT] obtain an admin token (POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token, grant_type=password, user admin)
[API] (step 2) POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/marketing/promotions {type:"DynamicPromotion", name:"AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-LASTUSE-<random>", isActive:false, isPublic:true, priority:1, isExclusive:false, storeIds:["{{STORE_ID}}"], startDate: one hour ago}; keep the returned id as PROMO_ID
[API] (step 3) GET /api/marketing/promotions/{PROMO_ID}; set the BlockCustomerCondition child to ConditionIsEveryone and the BlockReward child to RewardCartGetOfRelSubtotal amount 1 and localizedLabel en-US "1% off cart"; PUT /api/marketing/promotions with that body
[API] (step 4) POST /api/marketing/promotions/coupons/add [{promotionId: PROMO_ID, code: "AGENTTESTLASTUSE<random>", maxUsesNumber: 1, maxUsesPerUser: 0}]; keep the code as LAST_CODE; POST /api/marketing/promotions/coupons/search {promotionId: PROMO_ID, take: 10} and keep results[0].id as COUPON_ID
[API] (step 5) GET the promotion again, set isActive true and PUT it
[AUTH role=SALES_REP] obtain the rep token
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql/sales-rep salesRepCoupons(storeId:"{{STORE_ID}}", cultureName:"en-US", first:100, after:"0") { totalCount items { couponCode maxUsesNumber totalUsesCount } }; re-run every 3 s for at most 60 s until LAST_CODE is listed; record BEFORE_TOTAL, LAST_MAX and LAST_USED of the listed item
[AUTH role=ACME_BUYER] obtain the buyer token
[SETUP] step 8, the buyer order (the same mutations are reused by SR-GQL-174)
[API] as the buyer POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql with query { me { id } } and keep the id as USER_ID
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql mutation { clearCart(command: { storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}" userId: "<USER_ID>" cartName: "AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-ORDER" }) { id } }
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql mutation { addItem(command: { storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}" userId: "<USER_ID>" cartName: "AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-ORDER" productId: "@td(BUYABLE_NO_MIN_QTY.id)" quantity: 1 }) { id } } and keep the returned id as CART_ID
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql mutation { addOrUpdateCartShipment(command: { storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}" userId: "<USER_ID>" cartName: "AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-ORDER" shipment: { shipmentMethodCode: "FixedRate" shipmentMethodOption: "Ground" price: 150 deliveryAddress: { city: "New York" countryCode: "USA" countryName: "United States" firstName: "Test" lastName: "User" line1: "123 Test St" postalCode: "10001" regionId: "NY" regionName: "New York" } } }) { id } }
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql mutation { addOrUpdateCartPayment(command: { storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}" userId: "<USER_ID>" cartName: "AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-ORDER" payment: { paymentGatewayCode: "DefaultManualPaymentMethod" } }) { id } }
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql mutation { addCoupon(command: { storeId: "{{STORE_ID}}" userId: "<USER_ID>" cartName: "AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-ORDER" couponCode: "{LAST_CODE}" }) { id coupons { code isAppliedSuccessfully } } } and check that coupons[?code={LAST_CODE}].isAppliedSuccessfully is true
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql mutation { createOrderFromCart(command: { cartId: "<CART_ID>" }) { id number status } } and keep the returned id as ORDER_ID
[AUTH role=SALES_REP] use the rep token again
[WAIT] re-run the rep query every 3 s for at most 60 s until LAST_CODE is no longer listed; record SECS_TO_GONE, whether LAST_CODE is still listed at the end (STILL_LISTED) and AFTER_TOTAL
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] admin coupons/search for PROMO_ID reports totalUsesCount = 1 after the order
[API] the buyer's addCoupon response lists LAST_CODE as applied before the order, and a second addCoupon of the same code in a new cart is refused afterwards
Failure_Signals:
LAST_CODE still listed after 60 s (cached usage count, no fresh recount)
AFTER_TOTAL differs from BEFORE_TOTAL - 1 (another coupon vanished, or none did)
addCoupon refused before the order, so the case never spent the use and the absence below is vacuous
errors[] non-empty on a rep response
Cleanup:
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT] DELETE /api/order/customerOrders?ids=ORDER_ID, DELETE /api/marketing/promotions/coupons/delete?ids=COUPON_ID, DELETE /api/marketing/promotions?ids=PROMO_ID
[AUTH role=ACME_BUYER] clearCart for cartName AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-ORDER
If the case aborted midway: search promotions for the name prefix AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-LASTUSE and delete every match, then confirm no listed coupon name starts with AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-LASTUSE

Title: salesRepCoupons — order is soonest end first, no-end last, and the order inside a tie of equal end dates is the same on two requests
Preconditions: Procedural (agent lane): the runner grammar compares numbers, not ISO date strings, so the ordering is read from the recorded sequence. The tie claim needs at least two listed items that share one endDate, and the nulls-last claim needs at least one item without an endDate; the case checks both from the response and records BLOCKED, never PASS, when a tie is missing. When the stand holds no natural tie, the case creates one (two in-case single-coupon promotions given the same end) and removes it in Cleanup.
Steps:
[AUTH role=SALES_REP] obtain the rep token
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql/sales-rep salesRepCoupons(storeId:"{{STORE_ID}}", cultureName:"en-US", first:100, after:"0") { totalCount items { couponCode endDate } }; record the sequence of couponCode and endDate as SEQ_A
[KEY] record whether at least two items of SEQ_A share one endDate (TIE_PRESENT) and whether at least one item has no endDate (UNDATED_PRESENT)
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT] only when TIE_PRESENT is false: create TWO single-coupon promotions as SR-GQL-163 steps 2-5 do (no cap, names AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-TIE-<random>), both with the same endDate one day ahead at 23:59:59Z; keep their ids as TIE_PROMO_1 and TIE_PROMO_2
[AUTH role=SALES_REP] only when a tie was created: re-run the SEQ_A request every 3 s for at most 60 s until both in-case coupons are listed, and record the sequence again as SEQ_A
[KEY] record TIE_PRESENT again from the final SEQ_A; if it is still false record BLOCKED:CONDITION_NOT_MET naming the missing tie and stop
[API] send the identical request again and record SEQ_B
Cross_Layer_Checks: [UI] the widget's first N cards and the page's first ten rows are the head of SEQ_A (SR-CP-070); the last page of the page shows the coupons without an end date last (SR-CP-073)
Failure_Signals:
an item with a later end date precedes one with an earlier end date
an item without an end date precedes a dated item (the buyer path sorts them first)
the same position holds a different coupon in SEQ_B (unstable tie order)
errors[] non-empty on either response
Cleanup:
none when no tie was created (read-only)
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT] when a tie was created: DELETE /api/marketing/promotions?ids=TIE_PROMO_1 and TIE_PROMO_2 (their coupons go with them); if the case aborted midway, delete every promotion whose name starts with AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-TIE
References: VCST-6158 · AC-10 · Archetype:BOUNDARY · Technique:EP · Catches: the list reorders between reloads so the rep and the buyer read different coupons at one position · Behavior:sr.coupons · Observed: SBTM-VCST-6158-2026-11-03

Title: salesRepCoupons — a cancelled order does not give a capped coupon its use back and the rep count stays
Preconditions: Procedural (agent lane). Created in the case, deleted in Cleanup: a public single-coupon promotion whose coupon has a total cap of 3 (admin REST sequence as in SR-GQL-163). One real buyer order uses it once; an admin then cancels that order. PO-QUESTION: should a cancelled order give its use back? The product answer today is no (observed 2026-11-03 for 3 minutes; the marketing usage recorder writes on order add and removes none on cancel). The case records and asserts that observed behaviour so a change in either direction is noticed; it does not claim it is correct.
Steps:
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT] obtain an admin token; create the promotion and its coupon exactly as SR-GQL-163 steps 2-4 and 5 do, with maxUsesNumber: 3 and the name prefix AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-CANCEL; keep PROMO_ID, the coupon id COUPON_ID and the code CAP_CODE
[AUTH role=SALES_REP] obtain the rep token
[API] POST {{BACK_URL}}/graphql/sales-rep salesRepCoupons(storeId:"{{STORE_ID}}", cultureName:"en-US", first:100, after:"0") { totalCount items { couponCode maxUsesNumber totalUsesCount } }; poll every 3 s for at most 60 s until CAP_CODE is listed; record USED_0
[AUTH role=ACME_BUYER] obtain the buyer token
[API] as the buyer clear the cart, then place ONE real order that applies CAP_CODE (the cart and order mutations of SR-GQL-163 step 8, with CAP_CODE as the coupon); keep the order id ORDER_ID
[AUTH role=SALES_REP] use the rep token again
[WAIT] re-run the rep query every 3 s for at most 60 s until CAP_CODE shows totalUsesCount greater than USED_0; record USED_1
[AUTH role=ADMIN_DEFAULT] GET /api/order/customerOrders/{ORDER_ID}, set isCancelled true, status "Cancelled", cancelReason "AGENT-TEST VCST-6158 cancel", cancelledDate now; PUT /api/order/customerOrders; record CANCEL_AT
[AUTH role=SALES_REP] [WAIT] re-run the rep query every 15 s for 3 minutes after CANCEL_AT; record USED_AFTER at each sample
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] admin coupons/search for PROMO_ID reports totalUsesCount equal to USED_1 after the cancel
[SOURCE] marketing CouponUsageRecordHandler writes usage for EntryState.Added orders only (main HEAD, not pinned to the deployed tag)
Failure_Signals:
USED_AFTER drops below USED_1 (the platform now releases a use: PO decides whether the assertion or the product is right)
the coupon disappears after the cancel
the order never reaches Cancelled, so the case never reached its own question
Cleanup:
[API] DELETE /api/order/customerOrders?ids=ORDER_ID, DELETE /api/marketing/promotions/coupons/delete?ids=COUPON_ID, DELETE /api/marketing/promotions?ids=PROMO_ID; clear the buyer's cart
If the case aborted midway: search promotions for the name prefix AGENT-TEST-SRCPN-CANCEL and delete every match
